candidate.background_need: Fictional vocational teams in Finland and Sweden teach similar repair skills separately. They propose a twelve-month shared learning pilot, but language support, partner commitment and recognition of learning remain undecided.

objectives.description: Establish joint design of a repair module by the two vocational teams.
Identify mutual learning outcomes between Finnish and Swedish participants.

preliminary_activities.description: Draft a joint repair module curriculum.
Secure preliminary Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) from Eastshore Learning Centre and Westshore Workshop.
Design a language support framework for adult learners.
Administer pre- and post-pilot surveys to measure communication skills.

expected_results.description: Completion of the joint repair module design draft.
Identification of mutual learning outcomes by participants.

proposed_indicators.description: Number of joint module sections co-designed and reviewed.
proposed_indicators.measurement_method: Count of distinct curriculum modules jointly reviewed by both teams prior to finalization.

proposed_indicators.description: Percentage score indicating improvement in cross-border communication skills.
proposed_indicators.measurement_method: Aggregated percentage derived from pre- and post-pilot survey comparison using a 5-point scale, measured at month 12.

assumptions: Funding eligibility rules for the Interreg-style partnership are finalized before pilot start.
Both Eastshore Learning Centre and Westshore Workshop commit to full participation by month 3.
Participants will complete the pre- and post-pilot surveys as scheduled.
open_questions: What specific language support mechanisms will be implemented?
How will learning outcomes be formally recognized across borders?
